blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Coordinating transport and logistics means being the conductor of a small orchestra. Trucks, ships, planes, carriers, customs agents and warehouses all have to play their parts at the right moment, or the whole piece falls apart.

Two habits keep the music playing. First, a calm, shared view of where everything is: a simple tracking board that everyone can see, updated often enough to be believed. Second, a small set of trusted carriers for each lane, so that when something breaks, the call is short and the backup already knows the route.

Although problems will always happen, the skill is not in preventing them all — it is in noticing them early and responding quickly, because a small delay caught at hour one is much cheaper than the same delay found at hour twelve.

items.q: What image does the author use for coordinating transport and logistics?
options: A conductor leading a small orchestra
items.why: "being the conductor of a small orchestra" — cada parte tem de tocar na hora certa.

items.q: According to the text, what makes a tracking board useful?
options: It is designed by a specialist team
It replaces the need for phone calls
It is updated often enough to be believed
It shows only the primary carriers
items.why: "a simple tracking board… updated often enough to be believed."

items.q: Why does the text recommend a small set of trusted carriers for each lane?
options: So that customs agents are not needed
So that when something breaks, the call is short and the backup knows the route
items.why: "a small set of trusted carriers for each lane, so that when something breaks, the call is short and the backup already knows the route."

items.q: The text suggests that the author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Having a backup carrier is worthwhile
A good coordinator aims to prevent every problem from ever happening
Early detection of problems saves money
Visibility matters as much as movement
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a habilidade não está em prevenir tudo, mas em notar cedo e responder rápido.

items.q: What does the comparison between "hour one" and "hour twelve" suggest?
options: Delays should always be reported to the client
Twelve hours is the maximum acceptable delay
Most delays happen in the first hour
The cost of a delay grows the longer it goes unnoticed
items.why: Inferência: "a small delay caught at hour one is much cheaper than the same delay found at hour twelve" — quanto mais tarde, mais caro.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver orientando o novo coordenador de logística. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, so it's Monday morning — this is where the whole week is won or lost. Grab a coffee, because we're going to walk the tracking board together before anything else happens.

See these three lanes here? São Paulo to Santos, the Rotterdam sea leg, and the air freight into Frankfurt. I want a status on each one before nine, and I mean a real status, not a guess. If the number on the board is wrong, everyone downstream trusts it anyway, so a wrong board is worse than no board at all.

Now, the primary carrier on the Santos lane is reliable, although reliable doesn't mean perfect. That's why we keep two backups warm. On a Monday I actually call them, even when nothing is broken, just to confirm they have capacity this week. It takes ten minutes.

Here's the logic I live by: three calls on Monday morning can prevent five emergencies by Friday, because a delay you spot at hour one is cheap, and the same delay at hour twelve is a fire. So update the board, make the calls, and then we start the day.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver want the coordinator to do BEFORE nine on Monday?
options: Book capacity with a new carrier
Email the clients a weekly summary
Get a real status on each lane on the tracking board
items.why: "I want a status on each one before nine… a real status, not a guess."

items.q: Why does Oliver say a wrong board is worse than no board at all?
options: Because carriers refuse to use it
Because everyone downstream trusts the number anyway
Because the software crashes with bad data
Because it takes longer to update
items.why: "If the number on the board is wrong, everyone downstream trusts it anyway, so a wrong board is worse than no board at all."

items.q: Why does Oliver call the backup carriers even when nothing is broken?
options: To confirm they have capacity this week
items.why: "just to confirm they have capacity this week."

items.q: What does Oliver imply when he says "reliable doesn't mean perfect"?
options: Even a dependable carrier can fail, so a backup is still needed
The primary carrier should be replaced
Backups are only for unreliable lanes
items.why: Inferência: por isso ele mantém dois backups "aquecidos" mesmo na rota confiável.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's approach to logistics?
options: Indifferent — he lets the carriers manage themselves
Proactive — he catches problems early to avoid emergencies later
Cost-driven — he chooses the cheapest carrier each week
Reactive — he waits for problems to be reported
items.why: Inferência: "three calls on Monday morning can prevent five emergencies by Friday" — ele age antes, não depois.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A good coordinator is the conductor of the whole operation." A conductor is…
options: someone who directs the many parts so they work together
items.why: Conductor = maestro: quem coordena as várias partes para atuarem juntas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We keep two ___ carriers on each lane, so a breakdown never stops the delivery."
items.why: Backup = reserva: o transportador de apoio para quando o principal falha.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The São Paulo–Santos ___ is our busiest route, with three shipments a day."
items.why: Lane = rota / trecho específico de transporte.

items.q: "Each carrier has to play its part at the right moment." This means each carrier must…
options: do its own job at the right time
items.why: To play a part = cumprir o seu papel, fazer a sua parte na hora certa.

items.q: "We only work with trusted carriers on the critical lanes." Trusted carriers are ones that…
options: have proven they can be relied on
items.why: Trusted = de confiança: que já provaram ser confiáveis.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem na coordenação de transporte e logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The primary carrier let us down, so we had to fall back on the backup." To fall back on means to…
items.why: Fall back on = recorrer a algo de reserva quando o plano principal falha.

items.q: "We will roll out the new tracking board across all three lanes next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A container was stuck at customs, and it held up the whole shipment." To hold up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, segurar o andamento.

items.q: "The coordinator agreed to check the board daily, but she never followed through." She…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's keep on top of the delays before they turn into emergencies." To keep on top of something means to…
options: stay in control of it and manage it closely
items.why: Keep on top of = manter sob controle, acompanhar de perto.
